SI-4_title.answer: Multimodal normative modeling in Alzheimer's Disease with introspective variational autoencoders

NM2-1_modeling_methods.detail: The study developed a multimodal soft-introspective VAE (mmSIVAE) for normative modeling across multiple neuroimaging modalities. The model extends Soft-IntroVAE (SIVAE) to handle multiple modalities with a Mixture-of-Product-of-Experts (MOPOE) approach for aggregating multimodal information in the latent space. The VAE is trained adversarially to enable the encoder to distinguish between generated and real data.
NM2-1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we developed a multimodal introspective VAE that enhances normative modeling by achieving more precise representations of healthy anatomy in both the latent space and reconstructions. Additionally, we implemented a Mixture-of-Product-of-Experts (MOPOE) approach, leveraging the strengths of PoE and MoE to efficiently aggregate multimodal information

NM2-2_response_variable.detail: The study used regional brain volumes extracted from T1-weighted MRI scans (66 cortical regions from Desikan-Killiany atlas and 24 subcortical regions) and regional Standardized Uptake Value Ratio (SUVR) values extracted from AV45 Amyloid PET scans as the two input modalities for the model.
NM2-2_response_variable.supporting_text: We used regional brain volumes extracted from T1-weighted MRI scans and regional Standardized Uptake Value Ratio (SUVR) values extracted from AV45 Amyloid PET scans as the two input modalities for our model (Figure 1). Both brain volumes and SUVR values were extracted from 66 cortical (Desikan-Killiany atlas) and 24 subcortical regions.

NM2-3_explanatory_variables.detail: The model was conditioned on age and sex of patients (represented as one-hot encoding vectors) to remove the effects of covariates from the MRI and PET features. Age was encoded as a one-hot vector with 44 positions (range 47-91 years), and sex was encoded as a two-position one-hot vector.
NM2-3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We conditioned our model on the age and sex of patients, represented as one-hot encoding vectors, to remove the effects of covariates from the MRI and PET features.
